title: An element good with respect to a maximal regular sequence of a Cohen–Macaulay module is a nonzerodivisor
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] (a Noetherian commutative ring with exactly one maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$). For a finite $R$-module $N$ let $\operatorname{Supp}(N)$ be the set of prime ideals $\mathfrak p\subset R$ with $N_{\mathfrak p}\neq0$, $N_{\mathfrak p}$ the localization [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], and let $\dim\operatorname{Supp}(N)\in\{-\infty,0,1,2,\dots\}$ be the supremum of the integers $n\ge0$ for which there is a chain $\mathfrak p_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak p_n$ of prime ideals all lying in $\operatorname{Supp}(N)$ ($-\infty$ when $\operatorname{Supp}(N)=\emptyset$, i.e. $N=0$; the same definition for any subset of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ in place of $\operatorname{Supp}(N)$). For elements $a_1,\dots,a_k\in R$ let $V(a_1,\dots,a_k)$ be the set of prime ideals of $R$ containing all $a_j$. Let $M\neq0$ be a finite $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] which is Cohen–Macaulay, i.e. $\operatorname{depth}(M)=\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M)$, where $\operatorname{depth}(M)=\operatorname{depth}_{\mathfrak m}(M)$ is the depth [def-weil-pbc-depth]; assume $d=\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M)$ is an integer $\ge1$, and let $f_1,\dots,f_d\in\mathfrak m$ be an $M$-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] of length $d$. Let $g\in\mathfrak m$ be *good* with respect to $(M,f_1,\dots,f_d)$, that is, $\dim\bigl(\operatorname{Supp}(M)\cap V(g,f_1,\dots,f_i)\bigr)=d-i-1$ for every $i=0,1,\dots,d-1$. Then (a) $g$ is a nonzerodivisor on $M$ (multiplication by $g$ on $M$ is injective), and (b) $M/gM$ is Cohen–Macaulay, $\operatorname{depth}(M/gM)=\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M/gM)=d-1$, and $f_1,\dots,f_{d-1}$ is an $M/gM$-regular sequence (a maximal one, its length being $\operatorname{depth}(M/gM)$; for $d=1$ it is the empty sequence).

proof.text: Prove by induction on n the stronger regularity assertion: if fs is an M-regular sequence of length n+1 in the maximal ideal and g satisfies the displayed goodness equalities, then g :: fs.take n is M-regular. The induction does not require Cohen–Macaulayness or a separately specified dimension of M. For n=0, write fs=f::tail and extract regularity of f. If g is not regular, the union-of-associated-primes characterization supplies an associated prime p of M containing g. An associated prime contains Ann(M), so the finite-module support characterization puts p in Supp(M). The maximal ideal m also lies in Supp(M) by upward closure, and contains g. Thus both p and m belong to S=Supp(M) intersect V(g). Goodness at zero says dim S=0. Every element of this ordered subset is maximal (Order.krullDim_nonpos_iff_forall_isMax), and p is contained in m by locality, hence p=m. But f belongs to m, and the associated-primes characterization contradicts regularity of f. Thus g is regular. Nakayama, in Mathlib nontrivial_quotSMulTop_of_mem_maximalIdeal, makes M/gM nonzero; its empty sequence is regular, so [g] is regular.

proof.text: For n+1, write fs=f::tail. The regular-cons equivalence gives regularity of f on M and regularity of tail on Q=M/fM; in particular Q is nonzero, and it is finite. By the support-quotient formula Supp(Q)=Supp(M) intersect V(f). For every j<n+1, intersecting this with V(g,tail.take j) gives Supp(M) intersect V(g,(f::tail).take(j+1)). The original goodness equality at j+1 is precisely the goodness equality required for Q and tail; natural-number subtraction simplifies the dimensions. The induction hypothesis therefore gives regularity of g::tail.take n on Q.

proof.text: Prepend the regular element f to the regular sequence g::tail.take n on M/fM, obtaining f::g::tail.take n on M. Permute just the first two entries with IsLocalRing.isRegular_of_perm to obtain g::f::tail.take n. This is g::(f::tail).take(n+1), completing the induction. Apply it with n=d-1, using d>=1, then the regular-cons equivalence gives regularity of g on M and of fs.take(d-1) on M/gM.

proof.text: The support-quotient formula and goodness at i=0 give dim Supp(M/gM)=d-1. The quotient is nonzero by its regular initial segment. The depth upper bound gives depth(M/gM)<=d-1. For the lower bound unfold the definition of depth: in the infinity branch it is automatic, and in the supremum branch fs.take(d-1) is a regular sequence in the maximal ideal of length d-1, so its length belongs to the set whose supremum defines depth. Hence depth(M/gM)=d-1, which together with the computed support dimension proves Cohen–Macaulayness and every displayed conclusion.

split_report.summary: Split following the proof of Stacks Algebra 00N4 (lemma-good-element, algebra.tex line 24985; tags 00N4, 00N3, 00LJ, 05BV, 00L3, 0B52, 00LK verified in tags/tags): induction on d, stated as P(e) over all (N, x_1..x_e, y) so that the induction hypothesis applies to M/f_1M; base case d = 1 via the kernel K of g; inductive step: M/f_1M is nonzero CM of dimension d-1 with regular sequence f_2..f_d (0B52 clause (2) leaf, 00LK), g is good for it, the induction hypothesis, then the swap f_1,g -> g,f_1 by 00LJ (leaf), and f_1..f_{d-1} is M/gM-regular, so M/gM is CM by 00LK. Statement corrected: d >= 1 added. SOURCE ERROR: for d = 0 the goodness condition is vacuous and (a) fails (R = k[x]_(x), M = R/(x), d = 0, g = x is good vacuously and kills M; also any field R = k, M = k, g = 0); the source says 'there is no case to which the lemma applies', which is wrong as written. The citer lem-weil-pbc-cm-module-good-element-nonzerodivisor applies the lemma only with d >= 1 (its step 3, after its step 1 shows d >= 1) and with d >= 2 (its step 7), so it is unaffected. Departure inside the node (below the unit): in the case d = 1 the source shows K has finite length (00L5), so f_1K = K and Nakayama gives K = 0; here K = 0 follows from Supp K = {m} and 05BV (m is then associated to K, so f_1 in m kills a nonzero element of M), using the existing Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-minimal-support-prime-associated instead of two new nodes (00L5 is not in Mathlib). Written out where the source is silent: m in Supp of a nonzero finite module; Supp M ∩ V(g) = {m} for d = 1; Supp K ⊆ Supp M ∩ V(g); finiteness of K; that M/f_1M is CM of dimension d-1 and M/gM nonzero; the identification of iterated quotients; that M/(f_1,g)M ≠ 0. No new nodes; every node cited is of unit sk-thm-p1 or a Mathlib leaf. What the citer uses ((a), (b) with depth(M/gM) = dim Supp(M/gM) = d-1) is proved.
